description: Per-key merge policy for ~/.claude/settings.json. Consumed by scripts/intelligent-settings-merge.py. Replaces the hard-coded REPLACE behavior in the deprecated scripts/merge-settings.py.

env.rationale: Kit ships broadly-needed env defaults (UV_NATIVE_TLS=1 for corporate-TLS proxies); user-set vars (e.g., NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) must survive upgrade.

enabledPlugins.rationale: User may have manually enabled plugins the kit doesn't ship (e.g., sourcegraph); upgrade must not disable them. Kit adds new entries but never removes user entries.

extraKnownMarketplaces.rationale: User-added marketplaces (e.g. an internal org marketplace) must survive an upgrade untouched, which the union gives. But for a marketplace the KIT ships, the kit's declaration wins: the entry carries the release channel as a `ref`, and if the user's older copy won, the channel could never move. That is not theoretical — `claude plugin marketplace add owner/repo@ref` is refused when settings still declares the marketplace without that ref, so user-wins made the prerelease channel unreachable for every existing install. To point a kit marketplace somewhere else, register it under a different name.

effortLevel.rationale: If user has explicitly set effortLevel, preserve. If absent, take kit default.

permissions.rationale: The permission mode and allow/deny lists are the user's call, and Claude Code only honours some values from user settings anyway. The kit reads this key (rule 20 depends on which tools a mode exposes) but must never write it. Listed explicitly rather than left to the unlisted-key default so that the decision is recorded, per this file's own rule that the kit does not introduce a top-level key without adding it here first.

statusLine.rationale: A plugin-provided statusLine command embeds that plugin's version directory, so it breaks on plugin upgrade and is the user's to repair. The kit does not ship one and must not clobber one.

default_strategy_for_unlisted_keys.rationale: Any top-level key not in this policy is treated as user-owned and untouched by upgrade. Kit never introduces new top-level keys without adding them here first.
